name: baseline-align
title: Number and unit on one baseline
summary: A run summary (8.42 km, 42:10 min, 5′01″ /km) twice: with the row's default centring the small units float at mid-height, with alignByBaseline on the number and the unit they share the number's text baseline.
prompt: A run summary card with three stats (distance 8.42 km, time 42:10 min, pace 5′01″ /km), each a big number followed by a small unit that sits on the number's baseline, with a label below. Show the same card with default centring above it for comparison.
teaches: Put alignByBaseline on every text of a row to line their first baselines up, whatever their font sizes
Keep a unit next to its number in its own small row, and lay the stats out in a collapsibleRow with spaceBetween so a narrow card drops the last stat instead of cutting it
pitfalls: Put alignByBaseline on every child of the row: once one child has it, a child without it is placed with its top on the shared baseline (Java RowLayout gives it an align offset of 0), so a unit without it drops below the number
With alignByBaseline the row's verticalAlignment moves the aligned group as a whole; it no longer centres each child on its own

Player status (2026-10-29): the C++ player aligns baselines; the TS player ignores alignByBaseline and puts the units at the top of the row. The Java layout harness (MockRemoteContext) measures every text 100×10, so it can't check baselines

Weighted stat columns (weight 1 each) never shrink below their content: when the card narrows the numbers overlap and the last unit is cut. Size stats to their content in a collapsibleRow (spaceBetween) so the last one drops out; a weighted child is never dropped by a collapsibleRow

snippets.note: 8.42 (26 sp) and km (13 sp), both with alignByBaseline
the unit's alignByBaseline, before its 3 dp left padding
the same pair with verticalAlignment center, for comparison

check.describe: Top card: km, min and /km float at mid-height of the big numbers. Bottom card: their bottoms sit on the numbers' baseline (C++: the 13 sp unit 15.1 dp below the row top instead of 8.8). Resized: at 540 wide the three stats spread to the card's edges; at 240 (and already at 300) the collapsibleRow drops Pace rather than overlapping or cutting the numbers, and the captions end in an ellipsis.
